overview: Experian is a global data and technology company built around credit bureau data, analytics and software, serving businesses (B2B) and consumers (Consumer Services) in four regions: North America, Latin America (principally Brazil), UK and Ireland, and EMEA and Asia Pacific. It holds proprietary data on over 1.5 billion consumers and 175 million businesses, processes 7.4 billion transactions a year on its Ascend technology platform, and serves over 155,000 B2B clients and more than 215 million free Consumer Services members. Headquartered in Dublin for tax purposes, operationally run from Nottingham, UK and Costa Mesa, California, and primary-listed on the LSE (FTSE 100) reporting in US dollars with a 31 March fiscal year end.

business_model.summary: Experian monetises proprietary consumer and business data through two business lines. Business-to-Business (B2B, ~72% of ongoing revenue) sells Data (credit bureau records, marketing/identity databases, vehicle data) largely on a transactional/licence-fee basis, and Decisioning (Ascend Platform analytics, PowerCurve decisioning software, CrossCore fraud prevention) via software/licence fees, consultancy and transactional charges. Consumer Services (~28% of ongoing revenue) gives consumers free access to credit reports/scores and monetises the resulting audience through monthly subscriptions, marketplace referral fees (credit cards, loans, insurance) and white-label partnerships. Revenue is a mix of highly recurring (subscriptions, licence fees, long-dated B2B contracts averaging 45+ months with Strategic clients) and transactional/volume-linked (credit pulls, marketplace matches) income, giving some natural counter-cyclicality (fraud/collections volumes rise when lending slows).
business_model.customer_type: Dual-sided: B2B (banks, fintechs, auto dealers, retailers, telcos, healthcare providers, insurers - over 155,000 clients) and B2C (215m+ free members; monetised via marketplace/subscription)
business_model.geographic_mix: North America ~67-68% of ongoing revenue, Latin America (Brazil-led) ~14%, UK and Ireland ~11-12%, EMEA and Asia Pacific ~7%

competitive_position.market_position: One of the world's three major global credit bureaus (with Equifax and TransUnion), and a leading provider in business decisioning software (vs FICO, IBM, SAS) and consumer financial services marketplaces (vs Credit Karma/Intuit, NerdWallet, LendingTree). Scaled #1 or #2 bureau position in most of its ~32 countries of operation, including Serasa Experian in Brazil (market leader) and recently expanded A/NZ position via the illion acquisition (4th largest market for the group).

moat_factors.description: >90% of Group revenue is linked to proprietary data combined in hard-to-replicate ways across 1.5bn+ consumers and 175m+ businesses; a 'give-to-get' data contribution model (many data suppliers are also clients) widens the data moat as scale grows

Decisioning software (Ascend, PowerCurve, CrossCore) and bureau data feeds are deeply embedded in clients' underwriting, fraud and servicing workflows; average B2B Strategic client contract length has extended to 45+ months with 100% FY26 renewal rate among top Strategic clients
Credit bureau status requires accumulated historical data, furnisher relationships and compliance infrastructure (FCRA, GDPR, LGPD) that is difficult for new entrants to replicate quickly
215m+ free consumer members create a proprietary, consented data and distribution asset (marketplace, Activate lender panel) that few bureau-only competitors can match
Cloud migration and AI-driven productivity (labour cost as % of revenue down >300bps over two years) support margin expansion that smaller regional bureaus struggle to match

weaknesses: Revenue concentration in US/Brazil/UK credit cycles; B2B Financial Services (~53% of revenue) is directly exposed to lending volumes

Consumer Services increasingly competes with well-capitalised fintech aggregators (Credit Karma/Intuit) in marketplace and identity protection, a space the company itself flags as having 'bigger competitors in recent years'
Long-term disintermediation risk from 'open data'/open banking frameworks that let newer entrants build alternative information networks bypassing traditional bureaus

AI could change how credit/fraud decisions are sourced and distributed (new interfaces, agents, co-pilots), a risk the market priced in heavily during 2026 despite management's rebuttal that >90% of revenue is tied to proprietary (not easily substitutable) data

growth_drivers: Ascend Platform expansion - cloud-native analytics/software platform now has 37 product capabilities, 121 use cases and 2,374 client-specific solutions (FY26), driving higher-value, longer-duration contracts and cross-sell

Consumer Services audience and monetisation expansion - free membership base grew from ~110m (FY21) to over 215m (FY26), with diversification into marketplace, insurance, payments, debt resolution and financial health products (5-year revenue CAGR ~11% in these adjacent end-markets)

Cloud migration substantially complete in North America (ex-Health) and Brazil by end FY26, reducing technology cost and enabling faster product development; migration broadly done bringing FY26-era dual-run cost drag to an end

AI-enabled new addressable market - management sizes a >US$15bn AI-enabled opportunity (through 2030, Oliver Wyman analysis) spanning agentic commerce identity ('Know Your Agent'/Trust Score with Visa, Skyfire, Cloudflare, Akamai), Ascend governance/fraud automation, healthcare AI appeals (Patient Access Curator), and embedding consumer marketplaces into LLM platforms (live with ChatGPT in North America insurance, UK scores, Brazil financial guidance)

M&A - bolt-on acquisitions expanding data/vertical capabilities: illion (Australia/NZ, FY25), ClearSale (Brazil fraud, FY26), Audigent/NeuroID (US targeting and fraud, FY25), KYC360 (UK fraud/compliance, post-H1 FY26); ~US$0.8bn spent on completed FY26 acquisitions contributing c.1% to FY27 inorganic growth
Verticals expansion (Health, Automotive, Agribusiness, Marketing Services) extending beyond core Financial Services client base
Capital returns - growing FCF (OCF CAGR 10% over 6 years) supporting both reinvestment and buybacks/dividends

business.risk: AI disruption of data/decisioning value chain
business.description: Market reaction to FY26 results (shares down despite a 'record' year) reflected fears that generative AI and agentic workflows could disintermediate traditional bureau/decisioning data provision over time; management counters that >90% of revenue is tied to proprietary, not easily substitutable, data

Credit Karma (Intuit), NerdWallet, LendingTree, ClearScore and others compete directly for consumer marketplace traffic and monetisation; company flags rivals have become 'bigger competitors in recent years'
Financial Services is ~53% of Group revenue; a pullback in bank/lender marketing or underwriting spend directly affects B2B Data/Decisioning volumes
Long-term emerging risk from new entrants building alternative consumer information networks on open-data frameworks that bypass bureau infrastructure

financial.risk: Net debt and rising interest costs
financial.description: Net debt/Benchmark EBITDA ended FY26 at 1.7x (2.3x pro forma for the new buyback and acquisitions); FY27 net interest expense guided to US$250-260m, up from ~US$190m in FY26, reflecting higher average borrowings and acquisition financing

US dollar reporting currency with meaningful Brazilian real and UK sterling exposure; a ±10% move in BRL or GBP would move Benchmark EPS by roughly ±2c or ±1c respectively; FY27 guidance embeds a 1-2% FX headwind/benefit on revenue and EBIT
Non-cash FX gains/losses on Brazilian real intra-Group funding create statutory PBT volatility distinct from Benchmark earnings

regulatory.description: CFPB sued Experian Information Solutions in January 2025 alleging 'sham investigations' of consumer credit-report disputes under FCRA/CFPA; case remained in active discovery/pretrial motions through early 2026; Experian is defending vigorously, exposure includes potential fines, consumer redress and injunctive changes to dispute-handling practices

regulatory.risk: US state and federal privacy/credit regulation
regulatory.description: Proliferating US state privacy laws (e.g., California Delete Act effective August 2026) and proposed FCRA reinterpretations (medical debt reporting restrictions, data-sharing consent rules) could raise compliance costs and restrict Marketing Services/Data products

LGPD enforcement by ANPD and Central Bank of Brazil supervisory examinations of payments/credit businesses create compliance and litigation risk, including rising individual consumer case volumes tied to Limpa Nome and credit reference products
FCA's Credit Information Market Study is creating a new industry Credit Reporting Governance Body that could reshape bureau competitive dynamics and data-sharing obligations in the UK
EU regulation of AI and ongoing GDPR/Court of Justice rulings could affect credit scoring methodology and cross-border data use in European markets

macro.description: A substantial change in US, Brazil or UK credit/lending markets, or a sustained rise in interest rates curbing consumer borrowing and bank marketing spend, would directly reduce Financial Services B2B and Consumer Services marketplace revenue; flagged by the Board as an 'increasing' risk trend in FY25/26

macro.risk: Macro weakness in UK and Brazil
macro.description: Subdued UK economic backdrop and high Brazilian interest rates/inflation have weighed on B2B organic growth in those regions (UK B2B flat to slightly negative; Brazil B2B organic growth flat in H1 FY26)
Operating in 32 countries exposes the group to tariff and geopolitical shifts; flagged as an emerging risk layered onto the macroeconomic principal risk

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global credit information and analytics services industry is structurally growing, underpinned by rising credit penetration in developing markets (Brazil, India, LatAm), increasing fraud/identity verification needs, and growing demand for embedded decisioning software; management sizes total addressable market expansion to >US$155bn including AI-enabled use cases
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - B2B Financial Services revenue correlates with lending/mortgage volumes and bank marketing spend, but Experian's mix of transactional, subscription and long-term contracted revenue, plus counter-cyclical products (fraud, debt resolution/collections), dampens pure credit-cycle cyclicality relative to banks themselves
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - higher base rates can suppress mortgage/lending origination volumes (a Data/Decisioning revenue driver) while also raising Experian's own borrowing costs on its bond-funded balance sheet (net debt ~1.7x EBITDA, rising to ~2.3x pro forma for buybacks/M&A)
key_input_costs: Technology/cloud infrastructure spend (capex 8-9% of revenue trending to ~7% medium-term)
Data acquisition/licensing costs from third-party data furnishers

recent_developments.event: FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) preliminary results: total revenue +13% actual FX to US$8,425m, organic revenue growth +8% (top end of guidance), Benchmark EBIT +15% to US$2,407m, Benchmark EBIT margin 28.6% (+60bps constant FX, exceeding target for 2nd consecutive year), Benchmark EPS +15% to USc179.8, statutory PBT +26% to US$1,951m, total dividend +11% to USc69.25, cash conversion 93%, ROCE 17.2%. Announced new US$1bn share repurchase programme (to 30 June 2027), following US$725m repurchased in FY26 (incl. US$529m under the January 2026 US$1bn programme)

FY27 guidance issued: organic revenue growth 6-8% (midpoint 7% below consensus ~8%), total revenue growth 8-11%, Benchmark EBIT margin improvement of c.+50bps, double-digit Benchmark EPS growth, net interest US$250-260m, tax rate c.26%, capex c.8% of revenue

Shares fell on the results day despite the strong print and new buyback; analysts (Stifel, UBS) attributed the move to investor concerns about AI disrupting the data/decisioning business model rather than to the reported numbers, which beat expectations; stock was down materially (~19% at one point) on a year-to-date basis amid the broader AI-disruption narrative

Q1 FY27 trading update: left full-year guidance unchanged after Q1 organic revenue growth; some commentary characterised the update as showing slowing organic growth momentum versus FY26's pace, contributing to further share-price weakness
Announced an initial US$1bn share buyback programme (executed alongside the FY26-ending programme), ahead of the subsequent FY26 prelims buyback announcement

H1 FY26 results (six months to 30 Sept 2025): organic revenue +8%, Consumer Services +9%, B2B +8%, Benchmark EBIT +14%, Benchmark EPS +12% actual FX; raised FY26 guidance to the top end of the prior range (total revenue growth 11%, organic 8%, margin accretion +30-50bps); completed ClearSale acquisition in Brazil (US$329m) and KYC360 in UK post-period
CFPB lawsuit filed January 2025 alleging inadequate consumer dispute investigations under FCRA; remained in active discovery/motion practice through early 2026 with no resolution reported

Includes c.1% inorganic contribution from completed acquisitions and 1-2% FX impact

Supported by margin expansion and share buybacks reducing share count

Consistent with FY26 guidance of c.26%

Based only on completed acquisitions; guidance to be updated as further acquisitions complete

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Brian Cassin called FY26 'a strong year of delivery and strategic progress,' citing organic revenue at the top end of guidance, margin target exceeded for a second consecutive year, substantial cloud migration progress, and high cash conversion supporting 'strong capital returns on a growing base.' Management emphasised AI as an opportunity rather than a threat, pointing to >90% of Group revenue linked to proprietary data, c.US$2bn of FY26 revenue from new and scaling products, and a >US$15bn AI-enabled addressable value pool identified with Oliver Wyman through 2030 (agentic commerce identity verification, Ascend governance/fraud automation, healthcare AI, and LLM-embedded consumer marketplaces already live with ChatGPT). Despite the upbeat tone, the market focused on FY27 organic guidance of 6-8% landing below consensus, and shares fell on the day of a record results print, reflecting investor concern about medium-term AI disruption risk to the core data/decisioning model.

bull_case: Resilient, high-margin, recurring-leaning business model with 19+ consecutive years of organic revenue growth, expanding margins (28.6% Benchmark EBIT margin, up from 25.8% in FY21) and strong cash conversion (93% in FY26)

>90% of revenue tied to proprietary data that is difficult to replicate, providing a durable moat against AI-driven disintermediation that the market may be over-discounting (shares fell materially in 2026 despite record results)

Multiple growth vectors beyond the core bureau business - Ascend platform cross-sell, Consumer Services monetisation of 215m+ free members, vertical expansion (Health, Automotive), and an identified >US$15bn AI-enabled opportunity set (agentic commerce identity, LLM-embedded marketplaces already live with ChatGPT)

Disciplined, returns-focused capital allocation - ROCE consistently in the mid-to-high teens (17.2% FY26), growing dividend (+11% to USc69.25), and now two concurrent/consecutive US$1bn buyback programmes signalling management confidence and FCF strength

Diversified by geography and product (B2B/Consumer Services split, cyclical and counter-cyclical products) giving some insulation from any single country's credit cycle, with further scale gained via illion (A/NZ), ClearSale (Brazil fraud) and other bolt-on M&A
bear_case: AI and agentic/LLM-driven interfaces could eventually commoditise or disintermediate parts of the credit data and decisioning value chain, a risk investors priced in aggressively during 2026 even as management disputes its near-term materiality

FY27 organic revenue guidance of 6-8% (consensus-missing midpoint of ~7%) and a Q1 FY27 update read by some as showing decelerating momentum suggest the exceptional FY26 growth rate may not be sustainable

Unresolved CFPB lawsuit (filed January 2025, still in discovery through early 2026) alleging systemic failures in consumer dispute handling carries tail risk of fines, mandated practice changes and reputational damage in Experian's largest market

Rising net interest expense (guided to US$250-260m for FY27, up from ~US$190m) and net debt/EBITDA climbing toward 2.3x pro forma for buybacks and M&A reduce financial flexibility if credit markets or macro conditions deteriorate

Heavy exposure to Financial Services client spending (~53% of revenue) and bank/lender underwriting activity means a sustained credit-market slowdown in the US, Brazil or UK would directly compress both B2B and Consumer Services marketplace revenue
Increasingly crowded Consumer Services competitive landscape (Credit Karma/Intuit, NerdWallet, ClearScore) could pressure marketplace economics and customer acquisition costs
